newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds climbed to record highs before Friday's close, inspired by positive news about a European deal on fiscal discipline after the launch of a single currency in 1999.
"This morning everybody was sceptical. But now they have to surrender to the evidence," a dealer in Madrid said.
As the long term bond future rose more than a full point, the 10-year spread over Bunds hit a record low at 106.
Diplomatic sources said earlier that the European Union had reached an agreement on a pact to enforce budget discipline after monetary union was launched.
From Dublin, German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said he was satisfied with the stability pact, sending a strong message to the markets that the Euro will be a hard currency.

Friday's news started with a lower-than-expected November CPI, with a year-on-year rise of 3.2 percent from 3.5 percent in October. This opened the door for the Bank of Spain to cut 50 basis points off its key money market rate to 6.25 percent.
But the most closely watched event for the bond market was the Dublin summit and progress on the so-called stability pact.
"Now we can see the long term spread over Bunds falling to 100 basis points," said a dealer in Madrid.
Dealers now expect the 10-year spread between Spanish and Italian bonds to fall to 40-50 basis points next week.

"In the last few days, the Italian market was the one to dip the most, so now I'd expect it to rebound more," a dealer in Madrid said, adding that Spanish bonos were recently supported by strong expectations of a reduction in the official rate.
The only risk seen on Monday was profit taking, dealers said. "At this point I don't see any other good news we could expect before year end," a dealer said.
